title: The Threshing Floor
lead: A flat, open place where harvested grain was beaten and tossed in the wind to separate it from the chaff. Threshing floors were places of work, of night watches, of judgment imagery (Psalm 1:4; Matthew 3:12) and, at Araunah's threshing floor, the site of the temple.

sections.b: Joseph and his brothers mourn Jacob at the threshing floor of Atad (Genesis 50:10–11). Gideon threshes wheat in a winepress to hide it and lays out a fleece on a threshing floor (Judges 6:11, 37). David buys the threshing floor of Araunah to stop a plague, and the temple is built there (2 Samuel 24:16–25; 2 Chronicles 3:1). Hosea condemns "a prostitute's pay on every threshing floor" (Hosea 9:1). The image of winnowing becomes a picture of judgment: the wicked are "like the husks the wind drives off" (Psalm 1:4), and John the Baptist says the coming one "will clean out his threshing floor" (Matthew 3:12).
